dosforge Windows bundle — third-party software notices
========================================================

This dosforge Windows distribution bundles unmodified binaries from
the following projects. Each is governed by its own license; the
full license texts are reproduced in the ``licenses/`` directory of
this bundle.

QEMU
----
* Files:           qemu-img.exe, qemu-system-i386.exe, supporting DLLs
* Upstream:        https://qemu.weilnetz.de/w64/  (Stefan Weil's
                   official Windows builds of QEMU)
* License:         GNU General Public License, version 2 only
                   (GPL-2.0-only).
* License text:    licenses/qemu-LICENSE
* Source code:     The corresponding source is available from the
                   QEMU project at https://www.qemu.org/download/
                   and is republished alongside this distribution
                   for the duration of the dosforge release cycle.

mtools (mformat, mcopy, mattrib, mdir, mtype, mdel)
---------------------------------------------------
* Files:           mformat.exe, mcopy.exe, mattrib.exe, mdir.exe,
                   mtype.exe, mdel.exe
* Upstream:        https://www.gnu.org/software/mtools/  (Windows
                   builds from MSYS2: https://packages.msys2.org/
                   package/mingw-w64-x86_64-mtools)
* License:         GNU General Public License, version 3 or later
                   (GPL-3.0-or-later).
* License text:    licenses/mtools-COPYING
* Source code:     Available from the GNU project at
                   https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/mtools/ and republished
                   alongside this distribution for the duration of
                   the dosforge release cycle.

Your rights
-----------

You may redistribute and modify the bundled binaries under the
terms of the respective GPL licenses. You are entitled to the
corresponding source for the binaries; the dosforge project will
provide it on request, or you may obtain it directly from the
upstream projects listed above.

dosforge itself is licensed separately under the MIT license — see
the top-level ``LICENSE`` file in the dosforge source tree. The
bundling of GPL binaries does not convert dosforge to a GPL
license, but redistribution of this composite bundle must comply
with the GPL terms for the bundled binaries.
